speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. Given your symptoms of generalized fatigue, severe pruritus, and abnormal liver function tests, I need to determine if this is caused by biliary obstruction, cholestatic liver disease, or an infiltrative process.

First, can you describe the appearance and consistency of your stool and urine, and have you noticed any jaundice or pale skin?

Also, to help narrow the differential, do you have a history of alcohol use, recent travel, or exposure to new medications or supplements?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) or Hepatitis C infection.

Your history of ulcerative colitis puts you at higher risk for autoimmune conditions like PBC, but your sexual history also raises the possibility of Hepatitis C. Can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, and have you had any dark urine or clay-colored stools recently?
